source_facts: Solactive considers various events as corporate actions for index maintenance.
Those events adjust the Index between two regular Rebalance Days.
Those events materially impact price, weighting, or integrity of Index Components.
Those events need to be accounted for in Index calculation.
Corporate actions are implemented from the cum-day to the ex-day.
The Index adjustment coincides with the corporate action's price effect.
Adjustments comply with the Equity Index Methodology.
The document gives each corporate action a brief definition.
The document specifies the relevant adjustment to Index variables.
Solactive aims for a generic, transparent methodology.
Solactive aims to meet regulatory requirements.
Solactive may deviate from standard procedures for unusual or complex corporate actions.
Solactive may deviate to preserve comparability and representativeness over time.
Solactive lists relevant corporate actions non-conclusively.

The list includes cash distributions, stock distributions, stock distributions of another company, share splits, reverse splits, capital increases, share repurchases, spin-offs, mergers and acquisitions, delistings, nationalization, and insolvency.
render_facts: Solactive’s equity index methodology for corporate actions is available on the Solactive website.
The methodology is intended to create and maintain a generic and transparent treatment of corporate actions.
The methodology is intended to be in line with regulatory requirements.
The relevant corporate action list is non-conclusive.

The list covers cash distributions, stock distributions, stock distributions of another company, share splits, reverse splits, capital increases, share repurchases, spin-offs, mergers and acquisitions, delistings, nationalization, and insolvency.
Any corporate action considered for index maintenance results in an index adjustment between two different regular rebalance days.
Any such corporate action has a material impact on an index component attribute.
Any such corporate action is implemented from the cum day to the ex day.
The adjustment day matches the occurrence day of the related price effect.
For each covered corporate action kind, the methodology contains a definition.
For each covered corporate action kind, the methodology specifies the relevant adjustment to an index variable.
A non-conclusive list is one that is not conclusive.
Deviations from standard procedures are permitted only under the methodology.
Deviations are permitted for unusual or complex corporate actions.
Deviations are permitted where comparability and representativeness are preserved over time.
